summary: Tenant snapshot sync socket leak causing elevated 5xx rate and API Gateway backoff loop
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-12 03:04 UTC we observed a sustained elevation in 5xx responses (502/503) for requests routed to tenant Acme Analytics. The API Gateway entered repeated backoff cycles and a subset of serving runtimes for the tenant showed accelerated fd growth and accept-queue saturation. Impact: customer-facing API calls returned 5xx at ~8-15% for a 25 minute window; streaming sessions experienced resets; some low-latency requests timed out. Scope: limited to prod-us-east and predominantly customers with scheduled tenant snapshot sync enabled (dedicated tenants).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Ensure a dedicated tenant with scheduled snapshot sync configured (tenant flag snapshot-sync=on). 2) At ~03:00 UTC trigger tenant snapshot via internal admin API POST /admin/tenant/<tenant>/snapshot/sync. 3) Generate concurrent small-embedding and streaming requests (~200 rps) against the tenant for 5 minutes. 4) Observe API Gateway 502/503 increase and runtime fd growth in /proc/<pid>/fd and accept_queue metrics.
logs_and_metrics:
- apigw: 2026-03-12T03:05:12Z WARN upstream reset for tenant=acme-analytics route=/v1/embeddings status=502 count=120/min
- serving-runtime: 03:06:01 UTC fd_count=16384 (baseline ~512) for prefetch-worker threads
- netstat/snippets: many sockets in TIME_WAIT and CLOSE_WAIT associated with 10.20.5.*; accept_queue length peaked at 256 for runtime-ephemeral-34
- tracing: high retry amplification from hedged-retry policy, observed backoff loops between apigw and runtime proxies
- dashboards: 5xx-rate (tenant filter) peaked at 14.2% between 03:05-03:30 UTC
investigation_notes:
- Correlated spike start time with scheduled tenant snapshot sync (snapshot process opens many transient connections to shard-aware prefetcher).
- Heap/CPU metrics of runtime processes stable; kernel fd exhaustion and accept queue backlog were primary failure mode.
- Prefetch worker did not close socket on some code paths when snapshot worker returned early (hypothesis: error path missing socket.close()).
- Apigw configured hedged retries + aggressive retry window; retries amplified load when upstream started dropping connections, causing backoff loop.
- Quick mitigation: temporarily disabled scheduled snapshot sync for Acme Analytics and increased runtime connection backlog limits to reduce immediate 5xx. This reduced 5xx-rate to <1% within 7 minutes.
- Affected code area likely runtime prefetcher: snapshot streaming path. Created internal INT-18290 to track runtime patch and load test changes.
workaround_and_mitigation: 1) Disabled tenant snapshot sync for Acme Analytics (admin toggle) at 2026-03-12T03:12 UTC. 2) Increased runtime accept queue and ulimit for affected shards. 3) Temporarily relaxed hedged-retry policy at API Gateway for tenant routes to avoid amplification. 4) Restarted 2/3 runtime replicas for the tenant during low traffic window to reclaim leaked fds.
next_steps:
- Merge runtime fix to ensure sockets are closed on all prefetch error paths (PR referenced above).
- Add unit/integration test to simulate snapshot cancellation and assert fd usage returns to baseline.
- Add liveness check to detect fd growth and restart affected runtime automatically.
- Review hedged-retry policy defaults for tenants with scheduled background jobs; add per-tenant retry profiles.
- Run controlled load test with snapshot sync enabled to validate fix before re-enabling for Acme Analytics.
